title: Open ends make a tower stretch
claim: Open ends make a tower stretch. In a hub-free parity law (knot graph: knots as vertices of degree 3, shared distinctions as edges, distinctions held by one knot as edges to an unconstrained outside vertex), substituting a connected gadget for a knot keeps the old knot as an implied check exactly when the gadget adds no open end; then the step is a conservative extension (implied checks among old distinctions unchanged), so in a tower without open ends the original distinctions stay a knot at bond distance 2 at every level and each gains new bond-2 neighbours at every level (collapse; the 2026-10-20 refinement is such a gadget). When the knot graph is a tree, the bond distance between two open ends is the number of knots on the path between them plus one, so the star tower has bond distance 3^k + 1 between its original legs.
failure_conditions: A connected hub-free gadget with an open end whose substitution keeps the old knot, or one without open ends that loses it.
A gadget without open ends whose substitution changes an implied check among old distinctions.
A cubic tree in which some pair of open ends has bond distance different from the path's knot count plus one.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite hub-free parity laws and their substitution towers; bond distance as in NATIVE-NETWORK-20261021-001.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: prose proofs; check.py runs four checks with rejected controls (304 gadgets, 1,560 conservativity comparisons, the G0 tower to level 4, 150 random trees by exhaustive search, the star tower to level 5); no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found: cut/cycle duality for Tseitin systems and subtree edge counts are classical; the delta is the reading (a substitution keeps its old knot exactly when it adds no open end, so the ruler stretches only through open ends) and the exact tree-tower bond distance.
